title: Structures of the Heart and Pericardium

items: Know the role of the cardiac skeleton.
Define the cardio-neural system and its formation.
Define the pericardium and its constitution.

blocks.text: Know the four layers of the heart wall
The heart is formed by 4 anatomical formations:
I- The cardiac skeleton or fibrous framework of the heart
IV-The pericardium or fibro-serous envelope of the heart
The cardiac skeleton is the fibrous tissuee, which surrounds the atrioventricular and aortopulmonary orifices. Role:

items: Provides insertions to the atrioventricular and aortopulmonary valves.

Gives insertions to the atrial and ventricular muscle layers. Constitution: 4 resistant fibrous rings: which surround the 4 orifices: 1. Right tricuspid fibrous ring. 2. Left mitral fibrous annulus. 3. Aortic fibrous annulus. 4. Pulmonary fibrous ring0 These rings are reinforced by fibrous formations, which are 03 in number: 1. Left fibrous trigone: between aortic and mitral 2. Right fibrous trigone: between aortic and tricuspid 3. Atrioventricular bundle: between mitral and tricuspid.
Makes up the heart muscle.
It is an autonomous striated muscle regulated by the sympathetic and parasympathetic systems.
IT is formed by muscle fibers:
Atrial fibers which form the atrial wall.

blocks.text: All its fibers are inserted into the rings of the fibrous framework of the heart. 1-Atrial fibers: Arranged in 2 types: a-Fibers specific to each atrium: deep divided into 2 groups:

items: Annular fibers: surrounding the orifices: atrioventricular, superior and inferior vena cava, coronary sinus, pulmonary veins and auricle orifices.
Ansiform fibers: attach to the atrioventricular rings. b-Common fibers: extend transversely from one atrium to another

blocks.text: 2-Ventricular fibers: Arranged in 02 categories of fibers: a-Fibers specific to each ventricle:

items: Deep.
Attached by their two ends to the atrioventricular and aortopulmonary fibrous rings.
They create loops which move obliquely towards the walls and the interventricular septum. b-Fibers common to both ventricles:
Superficial.
Surround and unite the 2 heart chambers.
Attach to the fibrous rings.
Head obliquely towards the tip of the heart, creating a whirlwind at this level.
During their journey, certain fibers are applied to the internal surface of the bag (formed by the own fibers), others form fleshy columns.
IT ensures the propagation and coordination of atrioventricular muscular contractions.
IT is made up of a particular muscular tissuee = nodal tissuee.
This tissuee is organized in the form of cell clusters (nodes) and bundles.
Formed by: 1-KEITH and FLACK node (sinusal or sino-atrial):
Located in the posterior wall of the AD, outside the superior vena cava.
In the shape of a large comma.
Propagation of the excitation crosses the wall of the atriums via the Wenckebach bundles (A) to arrive at the atrioventricular node
Located on the lower wall of the AD.
Has the shape of an ovoid mass with two right and left ends.
The right end: presents several fibers (fan-shaped) forming the ZAHN knot.
The left end: continues with the trunk of the bundle of His. 3-His bundle and its secondary branches (atrioventricular bundles):
Located in the extension of the atrioventricular node.
It is carried forward in the atrioventricular septum, then travels along the interventricular septum (membranous part).
At the antero-superior part, the bundle of His divides into 2 branches (secondary bundles) right and left.
The 2 bundles develop into the ventricular walls in Purkinje networks.
Constitutes the internal tunic of the heart.
It is thin and covers all the internal surfaces of the heart chambers.
IT separates the blood from the myocardium, IT is in contact with the blood.
Fibro-serous envelope, It surrounds the heart.
It forms a real closed bag containing a layer of liquid which serves to lubricate and allow the mobility of the heart.
The pericardium is an inextensible sac (unchanged volume) hence the risk of pericarditis (inflammation: ?volume of the liquid)

It is made up of 2 parts: A- Serous pericardium (epicardium): It is the deepest layer, made up of 2 layers: The 02 layers delimit the pericardial cavity contains lubricating liquid to avoid friction during contractions 1-Visceral sheet:
Lines the external surfaces of the heart.
Is reflected at the base on the fibrous pericardium, thus becoming a parietal layer and covers the cavities
Behind, it does not completely cover the atriums, hence a region devoid of pericardium = posterior mesocardium.

The posterior mesocardium is made up of 3 portions: 1. Horizontal: between right and left upper pulmonary veins (a). 2. Left vertical: surrounding the 2 left pulmonary veins (b). 3. Straight vertical: extends from the cranial vena cava to the caudal vena cava and surrounds the veins right lungs (c).
IT arises from the reflection of the visceral layer at the base of the heart.
The serous pericardium lines the ventricles and extends onto:
Arterial pedicle (aorta and pulmonary artery) forming the arterial sheath.
Atriums
Venous pedicle (vena cava and pulmonary veins) forming the venous sheath.
The lines of reflection of the serous pericardium: are the 02 arterial and venous sheaths:
Arterial sheath surrounds the arterial pedicle.

Venous sheath surrounds the venous pedicle. The reflection lines form dead ends (recess) or sinuses between the vessels: 1- Haller's sinus: (oblique) of the pericardium which insinuates between the right and left pulmonary veins on the posterior wall of the AG, in relation to the esophagus. 2- Transverse sinus (THEILE): between the 2 arterial and venous sheaths, open to the right and left.
It is a closed fibrous bag which fixes and protects the heart.
Thick and resistant, pearly white.
In the shape of a cone with 3 faces, a top and a base
In front, IT goes up in the middle to the origin of the Brachiocephalic arterial trunk (born from the aorta)
Backwards to above the cul de sac of Haller. It is connected to the different walls of the thorax and neighboring organs by the following fibrous pericardial ligaments:
Vertebro-pericardial.
Lower and upper pericardial sterno.
Phreno-pericardial (connects the heart to the diaphragm). Relations of the heart: Are made via the pericardium:
Behind: are the relations of the AG: esophagus, thoracic aorta, azygos veins, vagus nerves, thoracic duct.
Laterally: mediatisnal pleura and phrenic nerves.
Bottom: diaphragm.

Foci of cardiac auscultation: Forward: sterno-costal plastron, according to a projection area whose 4 angles correspond to the (orifices of the heart) foci of auscultation:

items: Aortic = right para-sternal 2nd right EIC.
Pulmonary = pulmonary para-sternal 2nd left EIC.
Mitral = 4/5th EIC under left nipple.
Tricuspid = right parasternal at the level of the 4th EIC.
